summary: Proved by Crew, Fan, Koerts, Moore, and Spirkl (Corollary 13, arXiv:2602.09863). Its out-neighborhood conclusion, by contraposition, bounds the global tournament clique number whenever every out-neighborhood has bounded tournament clique number.

since_posted.title: Characterizing Large Clique Number in Tournaments
since_posted.authors: Logan Crew, Xinyue Fan, Hidde Koerts, Benjamin Moore, Sophie Spirkl
since_posted.claim: Corollary 13 supplies a function h such that tournament clique number at least h(b) forces some out-neighborhood to have tournament clique number at least b.

notes: Corrected on 2026-09-10 following Samuel Coulomb's report; Corollary 13 was checked in the full text. Set b = t + 1: if every out-neighborhood has clique number at most t, the global clique number is less than h(t + 1). Thus g(t) = h(t + 1) - 1 works. The counterexample in arXiv:2401.07776 concerns the forest-backedge χ⃗-binding conjecture, not this statement.
